comparisons.peer_summary: The AMD Instinct family (MI200, MI300, MI325 series) utilizes CDNA architecture to address AI training, inferencing, and scientific computing demands.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific hardware technologies designed to address high-performance AI training and data-centric workloads in 2024. Micron (MU) focuses on the storage layer, specifically shipping G9 TLC NAND SSDs to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of AI training and machine learning. In contrast, AMD focuses on the compute layer, leveraging its Instinct family of GPU accelerators (MI200, MI300, MI325 series) based on CDNA architecture to address the same growing demand for AI training and inferencing. While both serve the AI training ecosystem, MU's disclosure centers on storage performance metrics (transfer rates, latency) for these workloads, whereas AMD's centers on accelerator architecture and hardware specifications.

sentences.text: In 2024, we also began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed to deliver the transfer rates required to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning to unstructured databases, self-driving cars, and cloud computing.
AMD Instinct accelerators are designed to address the growing demand for AI training and inferencing and exascale-class scientific computing.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data center and cloud computing solutions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers a deep portfolio of data center solutions including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SmartNICs, and FPGAs to meet performance requirements for data centers, supercomputers, and cloud environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures explicitly mention cloud computing and AI/ML environments as key drivers for their product portfolios in 2024. Micron highlights SSDs designed for 'cloud computing' alongside AI training, while AMD describes its data center portfolio (CPUs, GPUs, etc.) as meeting the performance requirements of 'AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.' Both identify the convergence of AI/ML and cloud infrastructure as a primary business driver, though Micron specifies the storage technology (G9 TLC NAND) while AMD lists the broader compute hardware suite.

sentences.text: In 2024, we also began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed to deliver the transfer rates required to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning to unstructured databases, self-driving cars, and cloud computing.

We offer a deep portfolio of data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers, supercomputers, AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.

comparisons.peer_summary: VeloRain uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures reference the use of AI or machine learning to improve performance in 2024. Micron states its G9 TLC NAND SSDs are designed to meet the 'needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning.' Broadcom (AVGO) discloses that its VeloRAIN architecture 'uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.' Both highlight the integration of AI/ML technologies into their product offerings to enhance performance, though Micron's focus is on the workload *being* AI/ML, while Broadcom's focus is on using AI/ML *within* its product (VeloRAIN) to improve distributed systems.

• VeloRAIN: Our architecture uses AI or machine learning to improve the performance and security of distributed workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss supporting diverse and high-performance computing workloads in 2024. Micron focuses on SSDs delivering 'low-latency and high-throughput' for data-centric workloads like AI and cloud computing. Intel describes its 'xPU approach' to deliver a family of products (GPUs, FPGAs, accelerators) that meet 'diverse computing needs' and 'increasingly diverse computing needs.' While Micron specifies the performance metrics (latency/throughput) for AI/cloud, Intel emphasizes architectural diversity (xPU) to handle various workload types, including AI.

sentences.text: In 2024, we also began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed to deliver the transfer rates required to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning to unstructured databases, self-driving cars, and cloud computing.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.

comparisons.peer_summary: GPU parallel processing capabilities are essential for deep learning, enabling AI solutions like generative AI and recommendation systems to deliver services difficult or impossible with traditional coding.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify AI training and machine learning as critical application areas for their products in 2024. Micron states that its G9 TLC NAND SSDs are designed to meet the needs of 'AI training and machine learning.' NVIDIA describes its GPU parallel processing capabilities as 'essential for deep learning algorithms' and powering AI solutions. Both disclosures link their core hardware technology directly to the execution and infrastructure support of AI training workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA offers a scalable data center-based simulation solution, DRIVE Sim, for testing and validating self-driving platforms and developing digital cockpits, supporting a software-defined approach that enables over-the-air updates for continuous innovation throughout a vehicle's life.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures mention 'self-driving cars' or 'self-driving platforms' as a key application domain for their technologies in 2024. Micron notes its SSDs serve unstructured databases and 'self-driving cars,' highlighting the data access requirements. NVIDIA describes its DRIVE Sim solution for 'testing and validating a self-driving platform,' highlighting the simulation and software-defined vehicle requirements. While Micron focuses on the data storage/transfer aspect for these vehicles, NVIDIA focuses on the simulation/testing infrastructure.

sentences.text: In 2024, we also began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed to deliver the transfer rates required to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning to unstructured databases, self-driving cars, and cloud computing.

In addition, we offer a scalable data center-based simulation solution, NVIDIA DRIVE Sim, based on NVIDIA Omniverse software, for digital cockpit development, as well as for testing and validating a self-driving platform.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures mention 'low-power' or 'low-latency' capabilities in the context of computing for advanced workloads in 2024. Micron emphasizes 'low-latency' for AI training and cloud computing SSDs. Qualcomm emphasizes 'low-power' computing via its Qualcomm AI Engine and Hexagon NPU for on-device AI inference. Both identify power efficiency (latency or power consumption) as a critical feature for supporting modern AI and high-performance computing applications, albeit in different device forms (data center/cloud vs. on-device/client).

sentences.text: In 2024, we also began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed to deliver the transfer rates required to meet the low-latency and high-throughput needs of data-centric workloads from AI training and machine learning to unstructured databases, self-driving cars, and cloud computing.

Our Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU is a key processor in our AI Engine and is designed for sustained, high-performance AI inference, enabling leading on-device AI capabilities with very low power consumption.
